name: Hada Labo hyaluronic lotion routine

card.summary: A Japanese-style routine of applying a watery hyaluronic acid lotion (such as Hada Labo's) in layers to keep skin hydrated and smoother-looking.

quick.overview:
Hada Labo is a Japanese skin care brand launched in 2004 and owned by Rohto Pharmaceutical. It is known for hyaluronic acid products, and its Super Hyaluronic Acid Moisturizing Lotion is described as Japan's top-selling lotion for seven consecutive years.

The routine uses a lotion, a toner-adjacent conditioner, to hydrate skin, which makes it look plumper and smoother.
quick.how: Users apply the lotion after cleansing and before moisturiser, sometimes in more than one thin layer. Brand materials emphasise simple formulas without fragrance, colourants or mineral oil.
quick.risks: Hyaluronic acid lotions are generally gentle; as with any skincare, users with reactions to a product's ingredients stop using it.

lead: Hada Labo (meaning 'skin lab') is a Japanese skin care brand launched in 2004 by Rohto Pharmaceutical, with a U.S. line made by subsidiary Mentholatum. It promotes a simple approach that leaves out unnecessary additives, colourants, fragrance and mineral oil. [1]
The brand is best known for hyaluronic acid products. Its Super Hyaluronic Acid Moisturizing Lotion is reported as Japan's top-selling lotion for seven consecutive years. [1]
The 'lotion layering' routine applies this watery product as a hydrating step in Japanese-style skin care, aimed at a smoother, more hydrated-looking complexion. [1]

angle.text: Hydrating lotions raise skin's water content at the surface, which can soften the look of fine dryness lines and improve glow.

paras: The lotion is a toner-adjacent conditioner that is a distinctive part of Japanese beauty routines. [1]

timeline.event: Rohto launches the Hada Labo brand. [1]
